Action Plan:
1) Initiate management for suspected dermatitis of the hands and arms with emphasis on symptom control and skin barrier repair.
   - Prescribe topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation (drug name not specified; dose/route/frequency not documented).
   - Recommend daily emollients to dry skin (ongoing, throughout the day for the next several days).
   - Recommend over-the-counter antihistamines for itch relief: Piriton or Loratadine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
   - Advise avoidance of potential triggers and irritants/allergens identified in the history (e.g., recent swimming exposure; consider coconut butter as a potential irritant/allergen).
   - Provide patient information leaflet about dermatitis.
   - If symptoms persist or worsen after about 1 week, return for re-evaluation.

   - Schedule a follow-up in 1 week if not improved or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Dry, itchy rash on arms and hands.
- Onset and progression: Began a few days ago, after swimming; has been persistent but localized (hands and arms); no spread to chest, legs, or face.
- Symptoms: Red, itchy skin; dry; no cracking reported; no fever, vomiting, or systemic symptoms; fatigue noted.
- Exposures/triggers: Recent swimming; used coconut butter for skincare without improvement; no new soaps/shampoos reported.
- Sleep/stress: Stress at work (teaching), long hours; patient feels stressed.
- Past medical history: No chronic illnesses reported; takes Microgynon (oral contraceptive pill).
- Medications: Microgynon.
- Allergies: Lactose intolerance noted.
- Social history: Lives alone; non-smoker; does not drink alcohol; no recreational drugs.
- Family history: Father with asthma; mother with hay fever.
- Other: Generally well aside from current skin symptoms; no other skin problems in past.

Objective:
- General: No vitals available in transcript.
- Skin: Patient reports a dry, itchy, red rash localized to hands and arms. No systemic symptoms noted. No other body areas affected reported.
- Other: No fever, vomiting, or discharge reported.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Dermatitis of the hands and arms (primary working diagnosis: dermatitis with rash localized to exposed areas; onset after swimming).
   - Working diagnosis/differentials (consistent with transcript and DDx):
     - Irritant contact dermatitis — high likelihood.
     - Allergic contact dermatitis — medium likelihood.
     - Atopic dermatitis (eczema) — medium likelihood.
     - Xerosis/dry skin — low likelihood as a primary diagnosis, but may contribute.
   - Investigations: None planned at this time.
   - Treatments:
     - Topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation (name not specified; dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Emollients for skin hydration (apply as directed; ongoing).
     - OTC antihistamines for itch: Piriton or Loratadine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Avoid potential triggers; potential irritants/allergens (e.g., pool chemicals, coconut butter) as identified in history.
     - Paracetamol not indicated.
   - Referrals: None at this time.
   - Follow-up: Reassess in 1 week if symptoms persist or worsen; return sooner if there is spreading, fever, or systemic symptoms.

- Allergies/meds reconciliation: Allergies include lactose intolerance; current medication includes Microgynon (oral contraceptive). No other medications reported.
